probe_corrections: An initial stability-result formatter omitted candidate labels; a corrected process-pair check confirmed all five candidates remained stable.
A combined state comparison initially keyed records by numeric PID rather than service name; the corrected service-name keyed comparison confirmed all four state-record matches.
observation_method.command_line_output: Only allowlisted manager/service identity tokens were recorded; raw arguments were not reported.
observation_method.environment_inspected: Only the XDG_STATE_HOME key of PID 6943 was checked; it was absent. No other environment keys were read.

findings.summary: All historical manager/service PIDs remain present and matched the observed sanitized command identity, executable, working directory, and start ticks on two samples. The four child service PID/start_ticks/cwd records matched services.json and the current source identity predicates.
findings.limitation: Process identity and record matches establish observed identity, not by themselves supervisory ownership or live Popen-handle/control authority.

findings.summary: All five previously reported PIDs remain present. None of the historical PID observations was contradicted by this snapshot; earlier application-readiness results remain historical and were not repeated.

Expected lease and control socket are absent at the current default state path. No matching manager file descriptor or Unix listener was found for either expected path. No control request was attempted.
Each recorded service is a direct child of PID 6943 and each service process group equals its PID; this matches the expected topology. A process parent relationship does not prove manager ownership.
missing_evidence: Manager-held Popen handle ownership cannot be established from the passive observation.
Original manager owner/startup session is not established.
The manager lease and control socket are absent.

findings.summary: Passive kernel listener records map all configured loopback listeners to the corresponding recorded service process PIDs.

Current supervisory ownership is not established. Manager process, child parentage, and state records match, but the expected lifetime lease/control socket are absent and manager-held process handles are not observable.
findings.safe_conclusion: Do not start a competing manager or infer ownership transfer.

findings.summary: The current on-disk manager source hash matches the prior audit, and the manager command references its path, but no evidence attests the source bytes already loaded by the process.

No supported manager-to-manager handoff or live process-adoption procedure is implemented in the inspected source/runbook. The manager source rejects adoption absent a validated transfer, while the runbook says handoff is not implemented.
Relevant test implementations and prior audit result records were inspected. No tests were run in this mission; test fixtures do not establish current live ownership or loaded source identity.
